  1. The retail price is NEVER about what it costs to build / ship / sell a product.
  2. The retail price is based on 'what the market will bear.' I.e. They will find a point where they maximize the revenue from # units sold X price per unit.
  3. That being said, engineering R&D+overhead is very expensive. The average consumer has ZERO idea how much really goes into R&D+overhead. (The consumer products you touch every day are the results of many millions of dollars of R&D.) Research / Design / testing / insurance / etc. all need to be accounted for in the end product cost.

So ... If you are selling 1 million / year of Glocks, then your R&D costs as a percentage of units sold is relatively small. But, if you are selling "thousands" of 50 CAL BMGs, then your R&D cost must be spread out over a much smaller sales base. So, per unit, the additive cost of R&D is much higher.
